reason: The cited evidence supports the use of laser cladding for repair and the concept of adding ceramic particles to cladding materials, but it does not mention high-entropy alloys in the context of repair, nor does it provide any evidence that an HEA composite coating avoids hot cracking or simultaneously improves hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance compared to fusion welding.
premises: Laser cladding provides low dilution, rapid cooling, and robust metallurgical bonding, making it suitable for repair.
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are a distinct class of materials suitable for surface coatings.
Ceramic particles like TiC can be used as reinforcing phases in cladding alloys to enhance surface properties.
The proposed HEA composite coating will avoid hot cracking, unlike traditional fusion welding.
The coating will simultaneously improve hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance.
